title: Mario Díaz-Balart highlights local achievements and comments on Latin American democracy
text:
Mario Díaz-Balart, U.S. Congressman representing Florida’s 26th District since 2003, used his social media platform to highlight recent events and express his views on issues related to democracy and justice in Latin America.
On June 9, 2026, Díaz-Balart congratulated a constituent for a significant achievement: “Congratulations to Cameron Hamilton from Naples on being awarded the Congressional Gold Medalist Class of 2026! It was a pleasure meeting Cameron and his mom during the Congressional Award Gold Medalist fly‑in in Washington, D.C. Cameron completed more than 400 hours of https://t.co/JupXtbIOGY”.
The following day, he commented on the release of Williams Dávila, a Venezuelan political figure: “¡Un placer conocer a @williamsdavila en libertad! Williams fue capturado violentamente en agosto de 2024 y encarcelado injustamente en El Helicoide, una de las peores cárceles del mundo, por defender la democracia y la libertad. Hoy está libre. Pero cientos de presos https://t.co/ik6F1i03mW” (June 10, 2026).
Later that same day, Díaz-Balart addressed U.S. policy toward individuals associated with the Cuban government: “¡Los esbirros del régimen castrista y quienes se hayan beneficiado a costa del pueblo cubano oprimido no tienen cabida en Estados Unidos! ¡Que se larguen de aquí o enfrenten la justicia y la rendición de cuentas, como hemos visto recientemente con la hija de un general https://t.co/a4j8crVvBF https://t.co/9lmgoWPrMO”.
Díaz-Balart has represented Florida’s 26th District in Congress since 2003 and previously served in both chambers of the Florida legislature. Born in Fort Lauderdale in 1961 and currently residing in Miami, he holds a bachelor’s degree from the University of South Florida.
